title: On the uniqueness of the strictly convex quadrilateral central configuration with a fixed angle

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Lemma 2, Section 2.3 (display of ζ1, ζ2, ζ3, ζ4)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states ζ1 = R13 − 2η = m1m3/r13^3 (and similarly ζ2=m1m4/r14^3, ζ3=m2m3/r23^3, ζ4=m2m4/r24^3). Using the stated definitions S_ij = m_i m_j r_ij(δ − r_ij^{-3}), R_ij = m_i m_j(δ + 2/r_ij^3), and the critical-point equation S13 − 2η r13 = 0 (so 2η = m1m3(δ − r13^{-3})), one obtains ζ1 = R13 − 2η = m1m3(δ+2/r13^3) − m1m3(δ−1/r13^3) = 3m1m3/r13^3, not m1m3/r13^3. The same factor-of-3 discrepancy occurs for ζ2, ζ3, ζ4. The stated values are off by a factor of 3 (though the sign/positivity conclusion is unaffected).

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Lemma 2, Section 2.3 (cosθ expressions derived from S12 and S34)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof states cosθ = −S12/(2η r34) = r12(R12 − 3/r12^3)/(2η r34) and cosθ = −S34/(2η r12) = r34(R34 − 3/r34^3)/(2η r12). Direct substitution using S12 = m1m2 r12(δ − r12^{-3}) and R12 = m1m2(δ+2/r12^3) gives S12 = r12(R12 − 3 m1m2 /r12^3), so −S12/(2η r34) = −r12(R12 − 3m1m2/r12^3)/(2η r34). The displayed result both omits the mass product m1m2 (resp. m3m4) multiplying the '3/r_ij^3' term and drops the leading negative sign, making the stated equalities mathematically inconsistent with the definitions given earlier in the same proof.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Lemma 2, formula for a0 = ζ5·ζ6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Since ζ5, ζ6 are eigenvalues of the 2×2 block [[R12, 2η cosθ],[2η cosθ, R34]], their product (the determinant) should simply be R12 R34 − 4η^2 cos^2θ. However, the paper writes a0 = 4 r12^3 r13^6 r14^6 r23^6 r24^6 r34^3 (R12 R34 − 4η^2 r12^3 r34^3 cos^2θ), introducing an unexplained and dimensionally inconsistent prefactor involving r13^6, r14^6, r23^6, r24^6 that have no connection to the 2×2 block being diagonalized (which only involves r12, r34, θ). This formula does not follow from the stated Hessian structure.
